statement: In 7 adults with recreational MDMA experience (one double-blind, placebo-controlled sleep-laboratory study with counterbalanced sessions), a single dose of pure MDMA taken before a night in the laboratory, compared with placebo, is associated with about two hours less sleep that night (311 against 437 minutes), mainly because falling asleep took much longer (112 against 15 minutes), and with REM (dreaming) sleep almost disappearing (3.5% against 19.2% of sleep); light sleep rose slightly and deep sleep did not change. On the following night, with placebo, REM sleep was 22% against 21% after the placebo session, and no difference between the sessions was found that night. REM sleep was also lower than after a night of shortened sleep, so the REM loss was not only a result of sleeping less. The study had 7 people, one dose, and a quiet laboratory with a bedtime earlier than the participants' usual one (which the authors judged unlikely to change the comparison with placebo), unlike nights out with dancing, heat, other drugs or no sleep at all. The abstract also reports less deep sleep after MDMA, which the study's own results do not show. Certainty: very low. Status: single study.
plain: In a sleep laboratory, seven people slept about two hours less after a dose of MDMA than after a dummy pill, mostly because they took much longer to fall asleep, and their dreaming (REM) sleep almost disappeared that night. A night of short sleep without MDMA did not remove dreaming sleep in the same way. The next night, sleep was back to normal. Only seven people took part, with one dose in a quiet lab, which is very different from a night out.
population: Adults aged 19 to 34 (5 men, 2 women) with at least three recent recreational MDMA uses (lifetime mean 27), screened free of psychiatric disorders and drug or alcohol dependence
exposure: A single oral dose of pure MDMA given by the researchers before a night in the sleep laboratory (amount and timing are study conditions in the study card)
comparator: The same people's placebo night; as a positive control, a placebo night with a shortened time in bed
outcome: Polysomnographic sleep that night and on the following night: total sleep, time to fall asleep, sleep stages including REM sleep
magnitude: Treatment night, MDMA against placebo (mean, SEM): total sleep 310.6 (45.3) against 437.1 (8.1) minutes, F(1,6) = 8.6, P = 0.026; latency to persistent sleep 112.3 (46.1) against 14.9 (5.0) minutes, P = 0.038; REM 3.5% (2.1) against 19.2% (2.0), P = 0.009, drug by night interaction P = 0.003; stage 1 8.4% against 6.6%, P = 0.022; stage 3/4 not different (P = 0.119). REM after MDMA also lower than after shortened sleep (19.3%; post hoc P = 0.004). Following night: total sleep 403.6 against 431.9 minutes; REM 22.2% against 20.6%.

evidence.locator: Results › Effects on NPSG, 1st paragraph; Table 3, treatment column
evidence.extracted: MDMA against placebo (2-factor analysis over treatment and recovery nights, df 1 and 6), treatment-night values: total sleep 310.6 (SEM 45.3) against 437.1 (8.1) minutes, F = 8.6, P = 0.026; latency to persistent sleep 112.3 (46.1) against 14.9 (5.0) minutes, F = 7.0, P = 0.038; stage 1 8.4 against 6.6%, F = 9.49, P = 0.022; REM 3.5 (2.1) against 19.2 (2.0)%, F = 14.28, P = 0.009, reduced on the treatment night only (interaction F = 23.70, P = 0.003); no effect on wake after persistent sleep, stage 2 (P = 0.267), stage 3/4 (P = 0.119) or REM latency (P = 0.589).

evidence.locator: Results › Effects on NPSG, 2nd paragraph; Figure 3 legend; Table 3
evidence.extracted: On the treatment night, REM percentage after MDMA was lower than after both shortened sleep (19.3%; P = 0.004) and placebo (P = 0.004) (F(2,12) = 15.036), which the authors read as a specific REM-suppressing effect beyond sleep loss.

evidence.locator: Table 3, recovery column; Results › Effects on NPSG, 1st paragraph
evidence.extracted: Recovery night with placebo after the MDMA session: total sleep 403.6 (SEM 34.4) minutes and REM 22.2% (1.5), against 431.9 minutes and 20.6% on the recovery night of the placebo session; no main effects of night and no night-by-drug interactions except for REM percentage, reduced on the treatment night only.

evidence.locator: Methods › Experimental Procedures, 1st paragraph; Discussion, 9th paragraph; Abstract › Measurements and Results
evidence.extracted: Only 7 completed; two withdrew and the 12-sequence Latin square was incomplete; the laboratory schedule was earlier than the participants' usual sleep times, which the authors judged unlikely to affect the MDMA-placebo comparison. The abstract states that MDMA reduced stage 3/4 sleep, which the drug comparison does not show (P = 0.119).

risk_of_bias.note: Incomplete Latin square, two of nine withdrew, blinding of a noticeable drug not checked; objective outcomes.

indirectness.note: Worded for one laboratory dose with a full night in bed.

grade.reasoning: A placebo-controlled within-person laboratory study with counterbalanced order starts high. Risk of bias -1 (incomplete counterbalancing, two withdrawals, blinding not checked, a misreported result in the abstract). Imprecision -2 (7 people, one study, no intervals). Very low, although the REM effect is large and plausible. Single study.
